Subject: Intro + request: Redwood validation for Zenwood connector

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this — I'm Alice, lead integrations at Zenwood. We're evaluating Redwood Inference as the runtime for a managed inference offering we plan to surface to our ISV customers. High-level ask: can Redwood do a technical validation of our proposed connector and reference architecture (on EKS + GPU instances) and sign off on any required compatibility work?

Key concerns: model shard/quantization compatibility, KV cache behavior across short-lived sessions, and recommended routing/fallback if dedicated pools are saturated. We'd like a short architecture review + a reproducible smoke test matrix.

Proposed timeline: validation kickoff next week, short 60–90m architecture call, then a 2-week lab validation run.

Are you the right person to coordinate? If not, could you loop in whoever owns partner validations?

Thanks — attaching our draft reference architecture and an API spec for the connector.

Attachments (stub): zenwood-reference-arch.pdf (11 pages), api-spec.yaml (3 KB)

—
Alice Park
Lead, Integrations
Zenwood Solutions

Hi Alice — great to meet you (virtually). I'm the Partner SE covering ISV validations. Happy to run the tech review and coordinate a lightweight smoke test.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- 60m architecture review (we'll bring runtime + engineering): Tue 2026-05-12 10:00 PT or Wed 2026-05-13 09:00 PT — what works for you?
- We'll validate: model compatibility (quantized variants), prefix/KV cache behavior, routing/fallback options, and a short end-to-end sample using your connector API.
- Deliverables: a short validation report, a reproducible test matrix, and remediation recommendations (if any).

Looping in Marcus (runtime lead) and Olga (partner onboarding) to scope the smoke tests and outline infra requirements. Marcus/Olga — can you confirm capacity to run a 2-week validation beginning 2026-05-17 and whether we need any dedicated pool access?

If that works, I'll set the meeting and share a Drive folder with a checklist.

Best,

From: Alice Park <alice@zenwood.com>

Subject: Re: Intro + request: Redwood validation for Zenwood connector

Thanks Tessa — Tue 2026-05-12 10:00 PT works for our team. Confirmed attendees: myself, Ken (platform), and our SRE lead (Sara).

We've attached the reference architecture and API spec in case you want to pre-reads. A few clarifications that would help the call:
- Our connector will accept streaming requests and maintain short-lived per-session KV caches (30–120s). We use model variants in production: fp16 for larger models and int8/4-bit for lower-cost tiers.
- We expect ~800 qps peak for a pilot (burst to 1.2k) across ~200 concurrent sessions. Latency SLO target: 200–300ms p50 for typical prompts.
- We can provision a k8s namespace for Redwood's smoke tests or provide a recorder environment; open to your preference.

Attachments (stub): zenwood-reference-arch.pdf, api-spec.yaml

See you on the call.

—
Alice
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-15T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Zenwood integration technical vetting — internal checklist + gaps

Tessa — quick internal summary after today's readout and artifacts review. Forwarding the external thread for context.

Actionable checklist (high priority):
- Confirm quantization artifacts: request exported int8 and fp16 checkpoint samples from Zenwood (we have their api-spec but not the binary artifacts).
- KV cache semantics: run a 2-stage test (short sessions: 30s, mid: 120s) and capture prefix cache hit/miss and memory churn.
- Routing policy: propose a fallback plan — prefer cost-tiered fallback to smaller quantized model on overload; metric: tail latency <= 500ms during fallback window.
- Dedicated pool ask: recommend temporary dedicated pool (1 x A10 / 2 x A100 equivalent) for peak pilot runs; Olga, can you price estimate for a 2-week reserved window?
- Smoke test harness: build a cucumber-style checklist with 8 tests (connectivity, streaming, kv-resilience, quant-switch, fallback routing, session cleanup, scale-to-burst, telemetry/trace attachment). I'll sketch the tests and share.

Open questions for Zenwood to close before validation begins:
1) Can they provide sample model artifacts and a small corpus for quality checks?
2) Are they OK with Redwood running an in-cluster recorder vs using their staging namespace?
3) Do they have any regulatory constraints (data residency, log retention) we should vet before test runs?

I'll prepare the validation runbook and the test matrix by EOD Mon 2026-05-18. Olga, Marcus: please add any missing items.

—Marcus
Runtime Lead, Redwood Inference
